subject: Energy
title: CANDU Reactors
description: A fast breakdown of CANDU Reactors for builders.

hook.text: Canada's CANDU reactor uses heavy water (D₂O) as moderator—allowing it to run on natural, unenriched uranium.

buildup.text: Heavy water contains deuterium—hydrogen with an extra neutron, which absorbs fewer neutrons than regular water.

discovery.text: This means CANDU fuel doesn't need enrichment—simplifying the fuel cycle and reducing proliferation concerns.

twist.text: CANDU reactors can be refueled while running—avoiding the shutdowns that other reactor types require.

climax.text: About 30 CANDU reactors operate in seven countries—a niche but proven design with unique advantages.

punchline.text: Heavy water, natural uranium—Canada's clever reactor.

quiz.question: What advantage does heavy water give CANDU reactors?
